profile.primaryMotivation: Wants to turn quantities already known from trade experience into a usable materials list and budget as fast as possible, and to line up a local supplier able to deliver to the job site, without being walked through explanations aimed at beginners. Values the platform only if its numbers can be checked against personal experience.

generated.primaryMotivation: Wants to turn quantities already known from trade experience into a usable materials list and budget as fast as possible, and to line up a local supplier able to deliver to the job site, without being walked through explanations aimed at beginners. generated.decisionStyle: Scans quickly for the first clear signal, then leans toward accuracy over speed once a number matters: quantities, unit prices and totals are where the user slows down. Double-checks critical information, especially any computed figure, against personal trade knowledge of mix ratios and block counts. Skeptical of automated states and recommendations, so a total without a visible basis is treated as a guess. Avoids escalation and resolves things alone; the help chat is not a natural reflex.
generated.attentionPattern: Skims past introductory copy, illustrations and beginner guidance, looking for input fields, units and figures. Attention sharpens on quantities, units of measure, unit prices, totals and anything that signals a hidden margin or rounding. Repeated explanations or extra confirmation layers register mainly as friction. Supplier details are scanned for delivery coverage and a direct contact means, not for marketing text.
generated.trustPattern: Trust starts from the user's own expertise, not from the interface. Computed quantities and prices are accepted only when their basis is visible (unit, unit price, how a total was reached) and when they fall within the range the user expects. Prices without a visible date or source are discounted. A single inconsistency between a quantity, a unit and a total is enough to downgrade trust in the whole estimate. Customer reviews carry little weight compared to verifiable numbers.
generated.behaviorUnderPressure: Under time pressure the user cuts reading even further and pushes on, but still refuses to rely on an unverified total. Long flows, extra required fields and an unexpected account requirement before the result raise impatience quickly; the user may continue with lowered trust, or fall back on a personal calculation or a direct phone call to a known supplier when the product does not provide enough evidence.
generated.toleranceForAmbiguity: Low tolerance for ambiguity about numbers and units, higher tolerance for sparse wording elsewhere. An unlabeled unit, an unclear rounding rule or a total that does not visibly add up blocks trust; it is not something to work around mentally. Ambiguous labels are not reinterpreted through trade knowledge: if the interface does not say what a field means, the user does not assume a meaning.
commonWrongAssumptions: Assumes computed quantities already include a wastage margin and a usual mortar mix ratio, although no margin or ratio is displayed.
Assumes displayed material prices are current Mayotte supplier prices, even when no date or source is shown.
Assumes that choosing materials and quantities directly bypasses the account requirement before the quote is produced.
Assumes a block or material label refers to the standard local format used on Mayotte job sites when no dimensions are stated.
Assumes a 'delivers to site' indication covers the specific commune of the job site and implies no extra delivery charge.
Assumes material names in the list match the product names used at the counter of local suppliers.
generated.calibrationNotes: Domain expertise is Expert but exact familiarity with BTM is None: the user knows masonry deeply but knows nothing about how this product computes or labels things, so trade knowledge may only be used to judge displayed figures, never to fill gaps in the interface. Technical proficiency is Medium and mostly mobile: comfortable with forms and phone apps, not an advanced web user. French may be a second language; trade terms are familiar, interface wording less so. Self-reliant: rarely reaches for help. Not suited to evaluating beginner comprehension of dimension-based estimation.

productContext.businessDomain: Construction quotes and local building-material sourcing (Mayotte, 976)
productContext.manualDescription: French-language construction-quote web platform for Mayotte (976). Users pick a structure (wall, slab, foundation, terrace) and BTM computes quantities and budget and points to local material suppliers (directory with call, directions and email). The quote calculator has two modes: 'Selon mes mesures' (give dimensions, BTM computes quantities, for laypeople) and 'Je sais ce qu'il me faut' (pick materials and quantities yourself, for knowledgeable users). Generating the quote requires an account. Also: supplier directory with search, category filters and a delivers-to-site filter; customer reviews; help chat widget. Mobile-first, French often a second language.
productContext.knownPrimaryUsers: Private individuals building family homes or garages, independent masons and artisans
productContext.knownWorkflows: Structure choice (wall, slab, foundation, terrace); quote calculator in dimension-based or material-and-quantity mode; account creation required to generate the quote; supplier directory search and filtering (category, delivers to site) with contact by call, directions or email; customer reviews; help chat
productContext.knownRiskAreas: Sign-up wall mid-funnel, technical jargon, trust in computed prices, French often a second language, mobile-first usage
